title: Hello, pocopine
excerpt: A Rust/WASM framework that takes the whole app — components, stores, server functions — and ships them under one Cargo project.
body:
pocopine is a Rust/WASM framework I started writing after getting tired of writing the same JSON plumbing between a Rust backend and a JavaScript frontend. The pitch is simple: declare your component in a struct, give it a tiny HTML template, and let the same codebase ship both a wasm client and an axum server binary.

No schema files, no TypeScript shims, no derived types that drift out of sync. One #[server] annotation compiles to a fetch stub on the wasm target and an axum route on the host target. The macro knows how to split.

title: Reactivity that borrows from Vue
excerpt: The engine under the hood is a thread-local dep map plus a microtask-flushed effect queue — Vue 3's ideas, translated to Rust.
body:
The reactive core is a straight port of Vue 3's tracked-proxy model. Every component scope gets a js_sys::Proxy whose get trap tracks the currently-running effect and whose set trap queues subscribers for the next microtask flush. Signals piggyback on the same dep map via a synthetic scope so there's one engine, not two.

The win is that Rust handlers mutate &mut self fields directly; the macro doesn't force the user to manually re-emit change events. Reactivity runs after every handler or after any explicit Handle::update — the path is the same either way.

title: Routing without leaving the builder
excerpt: The SPA router reuses the existing tag-mount pipeline. Path params become HTML attributes; the walker handles the rest.
body:
I spent a long time debating whether to do file-system routing, per-component #[route] attributes, or a central builder. Centralized won: App::new().route::<Home>("/").route::<BlogPost>("/blog/:slug") puts the whole URL map in one place.

The fun part is that path params aren't a new concept. When the router matches, it creates <blog-post slug="x"> inside <pp-outlet>, then lets the normal walker mount it — the same path that handles <blog-post slug="x"> typed directly into a parent template. Path params are just attributes with extra steps.
